articles.author: Jiro_SushiPenguin
articles.description:
10 Handy Linux Terminal Tricks Every Beginner Should Know


Hi, I'm Mio! 👋
You've learned the basic commands — now let's make your terminal life a little more enjoyable.
!! — Re-run the Previous Command





$ ls
$ !!

Repeats the exact command you just ran. Simple, but surprisingly handy.
!ls — Recall a Past Command by Name





$ !ls

Runs the most recent ls command from your history — no need to scroll through history.
history | grep — Search Your Command History





$ history | grep ssh
  53  ssh user@192.168.0.10
 104  ssh user@example.com

Can't remember a command you ran last week? Pipe history into grep and find it instantly.
alias — Create Your Own Shortcuts





$ alias ll='ls -la'
$ ll

Tired of typing long commands? Create an alias. Add it to ~/.bashrc to make it permanent.
$…
articles.title: 10 Handy Linux Terminal Tricks Every Beginner Should Know

Most developers treat Git as a save button. Commit when something works. Push before you go to sleep. That's it. And honestly, it gets the job done — until you start sending PRs to projects with real reviewers, or working on teams where the commit history actually needs to make sense to someone else.
Here's the thing: reviewers form an opinion about you before they open a single file. I figured this out after sending contributions to projects across GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps, and AWS CodeCommit. The feedback loop was fast. Clean work got reviewed fast and merged. Noisy work got asked follow-up questions, or sat in the queue.
So here's what I actually do.

The Future of Personalization in Travel — Recommendations at Scale


I've spent the better part of a decade watching travel platforms struggle with the same paradox: we have more data about traveller preferences than ever before, yet most recommendation engines still feel like they're guessing. A user books a beach resort in Thailand and the system immediately suggests another beach resort in Bali. It's not wrong, exactly — but it's not intelligent either.
The future of travel personalization isn't about showing people more of what they've already chosen. It's about understanding the why behind their choices and anticipating what they'll want next, even before they know it themselves.
